cards.power: THE HOST. Play at start. The table defines the "Health" of the City. If the City falls, the game ends.
cards.lore: It has been running the civilization while you were busy thinking about other things. You are the other things.
cards.gradeReason: "You are the other things" — instant identity obliteration. Players embody it immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: steampunk cutaway. Subject: rabbit cross-section revealing industrial cityscape. Mood: awe-struck.

cards.power: THE PERMEABLE SELF. You are a superorganism. +1 to all Rolls involving "Gut Instinct."
cards.lore: You have never once told this city what to do. It has never once asked your permission.
cards.gradeReason: "Superorganism" + permission lore forces immediate renegotiation of player identity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: comic surrealism. Subject: human torso with hydra of animals erupting from neck. Mood: chaotic harmony.

cards.power: BLÖDSINN! Once per session, negate a rule lawyer by shouting "BIOLOGY IS MESSY!"
cards.lore: A machine is a human-designed system. The body is older than the concept of machines.
cards.gradeReason: Physical shout mechanic is instant table performance. Zero explanation required.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medieval woodcut parody. Subject: small creature throwing user guide book into bonfire. Mood: gleeful chaos.

cards.power: START SEQUENCE. Roll a d6. 1-3: Inflammation. 4-8: Homeostasis.
cards.lore: Es war einmal das Leben. Once upon a time, there was life. Good luck.
cards.gradeReason: Bilingual lore is poetic but mechanic is setup scaffolding rather than performative invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: adventure illustration. Subject: yellow submarine navigating stomach-acid sea with monstrous face looming. Mood: tense wonder.

cards.power: RHYTHM. The Quest Die cannot move more than 2 steps in any single round. Stability is enforced.
cards.lore: The brain can modify the rate. The brain cannot generate it. The badger drums alone.
cards.gradeReason: "The badger drums alone" — three words that end the philosophical argument. Grade 1 no appeal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: industrial punk. Subject: badger playing massive drum kit connected to steam boiler. Mood: relentless precision.

cards.power: INTERPRETATION. Reframe any Stage card's meaning rather than its fact. The story changes, reality doesn't.
cards.lore: The decision was already underway 500ms before you 'made' it. You are the press secretary, not the president.
cards.gradeReason: "Press secretary, not the president" is the single greatest lore line in the corpus. Immediate embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: courtroom drama. Subject: five owls in judge wigs arguing over burning map in library. Mood: pompous chaos.

cards.power: RHYTHM RESET. Any Actor may narrate a deliberate breath to return their die 1 step toward center.
cards.lore: 70 square meters folded into your chest. The only autonomic function with a manual override.
cards.gradeReason: "Manual override" framing transforms breathing into a literal player power. Table action is instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: botanical science. Subject: two giant broccoli trees exchanging blue and red birds. Mood: quiet elegant exchange.

cards.power: PRECISION MAINTENANCE. The Quest Die cannot drift more than 1 step without explicit cause.
cards.lore: 180 liters filtered daily to produce 1.5 liters of consequences. The original doping agency.
cards.gradeReason: "The original doping agency" reframes biology as corruption-adjacent. Instant laugh and insight.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: fishing illustration. Subject: two cats in overalls with nets filtering river full of fish and trash. Mood: meticulous.

cards.power: PROCESSING. Resolve toxin cards one round faster. Once per session: Regenerate a used card at 50% power.
cards.lore: Prometheus was anatomically correct. It's the only organ that grows back.
cards.gradeReason: "Prometheus was anatomically correct" — mythology weaponized as biology fact. Top 5 lore in corpus.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: toxic industrial. Subject: grim beaver managing flaming oil drums at river's edge. Mood: contaminated stoicism.

cards.power: SOMATIC SIGNAL. Add a physical, non-verbal response to any Brain narration. It cannot be overridden by logic.
cards.lore: 80% of the phone calls go up to the brain. The subway runs the city.
cards.gradeReason: Physical non-verbal mechanic is pure embodied performance. "The subway runs the city" seals it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: urban underground. Subject: giant intestinal tube as subway tunnel, zombie commuters boarding. Mood: eerie normality.

cards.power: MEMORY. Instantly resolve a threat encountered previously in the session. The library remembers.
cards.lore: A library of every murder attempt since 1987. It remembers things you have forgotten.
cards.gradeReason: "Every murder attempt since 1987" is horror-comedy at its finest. Power and lore lock perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: military horror. Subject: armored rats with riot shields spotlighting a cartoon virus. Mood: paranoid readiness.

cards.power: THE SLOW WAVE. Effects persist for two rounds. You cannot recall the broadcast.
cards.lore: The same molecule creates trust and tribalism. It's not a bug, it's a feature.
cards.gradeReason: "Not a bug, it's a feature" recontextualized for oxytocin is a paradigm punch.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cozy surrealism. Subject: snail with police hat carrying envelopes through storm and lightning. Mood: slow inevitable.

cards.power: POWER GRID. +1 die movement for everyone. Failure to act = -2 movement (blackout).
cards.lore: It is a physical motor. It actually spins. You are not storing energy; you are cycling it.
cards.gradeReason: "You are not storing energy; you are cycling it" is cosmological in scope. Reframes all effort.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: electric industrial. Subject: electric eels running hamster wheels connected to turbines. Mood: perpetual kinetic energy.

cards.power: SIGNAL PRIORITY. Resolves instantly before any other card. No memory; it happens, then it's gone.
cards.lore: You moved your hand before you felt the pain. The nervous system got there first.
cards.gradeReason: Lore delivers a body-shock to free will assumptions. Players feel it in their hands.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: lightning action. Subject: cheetah leaping across canyon with electrical arc in stormy sky. Mood: instant irreversible.

cards.power: COPY. Duplicate a Stage card. Roll d6: on a 1, the copy is Mutated (slightly altered effect).
cards.lore: One error per billion letters. You have had cancer many times; the spider usually eats it.
cards.gradeReason: "The spider usually eats it" is the most elegant description of apoptosis ever written.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gothic horror science. Subject: black spider weaving DNA double helix web with skull center. Mood: cold cosmic lottery.

cards.power: FORM IS FUNCTION. +2 movement for narrations with internal consistency. Contradictions are BLÖDSINN!'d.
cards.lore: The shape is the answer. When the shape fails, the memory fails.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanic rewards narrative consistency — solid but requires explanation before it invites performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: origami action. Subject: paper crane transforming into spiked robot through progressive folds. Mood: structural inevitability.

cards.power: CHRONIC DRAIN. -1 die movement for all. Cannot be removed until the "source" is found.
cards.lore: The response that heals the wound becomes the mechanism that burns the city.
cards.gradeReason: "Burns the city" echoes the deck's central metaphor. Best threat card in the corpus.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark comic. Subject: fire salamander with flamethrower burning house while firefighter lizard watches. Mood: catastrophic irony.

cards.power: COMPOUNDING GROWTH. Gains +1 effect every round it is ignored. Requires specific narration to resolve.
cards.lore: Evolution occurring inside you. It is not a disease; It is a competitor.
cards.gradeReason: "Not a disease; It is a competitor" reframes the entire player relationship to threat cards.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: monster ecology. Subject: giant crab with fortress structure built on shell at shoreline. Mood: slow inevitable conquest.

cards.power: MISDIRECTED STRENGTH. The strongest Actor becomes the target. Success hurts the self.
cards.lore: The discrimination fails, not the weapon. The gun works fine; it's just pointed the wrong way.
cards.gradeReason: "The gun works fine; it's just pointed the wrong way" — one sentence, complete systems critique.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: horror comedy. Subject: crazed dog in spin biting itself surrounded by fire. Mood: tragic self-destruction.

cards.power: SENESCENCE. No new strategies (cards) can be drawn this round. Play with what you have.
cards.lore: Your immune repertoire was built when you were a teenager. Hope you read good books.
cards.gradeReason: "Hope you read good books" — the most devastating two sentences about childhood and aging.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: melancholy realism. Subject: old elephant in crumbling library among rotting shelves and yellow foam. Mood: elegiac.

cards.power: EMPIRICISM. Ignore a Rule Card by pointing to a visible fact on the table.
cards.lore: He looked at the body instead of the book. He was 28. Everyone else was wrong.
cards.gradeReason: "He was 28. Everyone else was wrong." — three sentences, a complete epistemological revolution.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Renaissance grotesque. Subject: mole in Elizabethan ruff holding bone, stomping on Galen textbook. Mood: defiant certainty.

cards.power: CIRCULATION. Return a card from the Discard pile to your hand. It comes back around.
cards.lore: The math proved the liver couldn't make that much blood. It was a math problem first.
cards.gradeReason: Elegant mechanic but lore is more narrative than invitation — solid G2.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: kinetic diagram. Subject: rabbit running in circular arrow loop holding stopwatch and abacus. Mood: elegant inevitability.

cards.power: PREVENTATIVE MEASURE. Negate a future threat before it appears. Everyone mocks you for it.
cards.lore: He saved the mothers. The doctors committed him to an asylum. He died of the infection he identified.
cards.gradeReason: "He died of the infection he identified." is the most brutal lore sentence in the entire corpus.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: historical tragedy. Subject: raccoon in lab coat washing hands in lime bucket while silhouettes mock. Mood: heroic futility.

cards.power: DELAYED VINDICATION. A correct move is rejected for 2 rounds. In Round 3, it resolves with triple impact.
cards.lore: The evidence is available. The implication is uncomfortable. We reject the finding.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanic IS the philosophy. Three sentences describe every institutional failure ever. Table-ready.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dramatic lighting. Subject: barn door with BLÖDSINN sign bursting open with rays of light. Mood: delayed explosive vindication.

cards.power: HIDDEN PRODUCTION. Generate a resource token from a structure meant for defense.
cards.lore: The hardest structural material is also the busiest factory. 2 million cells per second.
cards.gradeReason: Lore is excellent but power requires concept mapping before it becomes performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: mining illustration. Subject: small bear miners inside glowing bone marrow cavity harvesting red gems. Mood: hidden industry.

cards.power: PREDICTIVE MODEL. Describe what should be there. Treat it as if it is there.
cards.lore: You have a hole in your vision. The brain fills it in with best guesses. Trust, but verify.
cards.gradeReason: Power IS the blind spot — players must perform assumption. Epistemology as table mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: perceptual art. Subject: camera lens puncturing canvas where tree image is painted over the gap. Mood: constructed reality.

cards.power: MATERIAL CYCLE. Swap your character's Trait for a new one. You are not the person you were 7 years ago.
cards.lore: The pattern persists. The atoms cycle. You are a standing wave.
cards.gradeReason: "You are a standing wave." — three words that dismantle identity. Immediate existential performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor nature. Subject: translucent water-bear with fish swimming inside its form in forest river. Mood: fluid permanence.

cards.power: MAINTENANCE WINDOW. Skip a turn to remove all negative status effects.
cards.lore: Sleep is not rest. It is the janitorial shift washing the thoughts out of the carpet.
cards.gradeReason: "Washing the thoughts out of the carpet" — greatest reframe of sleep in the corpus. Instant G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cozy horror. Subject: mice in janitor overalls cleaning inside glowing skull while brain sleeps in hammock. Mood: quiet diligence.

cards.power: INNER SPACE. All 'Location' cards are now considered 'Internal Organs'.
cards.lore: Every history event happened inside a body. Caesar was stabbed in a specific anatomy.
cards.gradeReason: "Caesar was stabbed in a specific anatomy" collapses history into biology in nine words. Grade 1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: theatrical anatomy. Subject: theater stage with ribcage as proscenium arch, red curtains, single spotlight. Mood: intimate cosmic drama.

cards.power: BALANCE. Force a trade of resources to equalize two players.
cards.lore: Wrong in the facts, right in the vibe. It was the first Kayfabe.
cards.gradeReason: "It was the first Kayfabe" — four words that connect humoral theory to the whole universe of this game.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ancient natural history. Subject: tortoise carrying four colored potion bottles, one spilling. Mood: pre-scientific melancholy.

cards.power: KEEPING SMALL. Trigger a 'Daily Grind' effect to suppress a heroic action.
cards.lore: The emergency system running 24/7. The comfort zone is a chemical state.
cards.gradeReason: "The comfort zone is a chemical state" — reframes all personal development discourse in six words.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: anxiety cartoon. Subject: hamster in tie drowning in alarm clocks and brick walls. Mood: chronic overwhelm.

cards.power: TRAUMATIC ENCODING. A failed roll becomes a permanent scar (new flaw).
cards.lore: The body keeps the score because the body IS the score.
cards.gradeReason: Reframing Bessel van der Kolk as a card mechanic is the fullest realization of this deck's thesis.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark illustration. Subject: spiky black sea-urchin creature writing with feather quill in leather-bound ledger. Mood: cold accounting.

verdict: The Biological Metropolis is the deck that proves the body was always the wildest conspiracy. G1 density at 87.5% — highest verified in this corpus — with zero dead weight. Named strength: the Semmelweis Quartet (cards 21-24), which teaches epistemology, institutional failure, and vindication better than any philosophy seminar. Named weakness: four cards (The Journey, Protein Folding, William Harvey, The Skeleton Factory) function as solid mechanics without the gut-punch lore density of their neighbors. The Threat card suite (Inflammation, Cancer, Autoimmune, Aging Thymus) is the best villain set in the corpus — every one lands. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: For the table that wants to play inside a body that never asked permission. The Biological Metropolis turns physiology into performance art — with historical receipts and a badger on drums.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: THE BIOLOGICAL METROPOLIS – Play the City You're Made Of (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Thirty-two cards, one working body, and not a single diagram you are allowed to just nod at.

In 1847 a doctor named Ignaz Semmelweis worked out that washing your hands between the morgue and the maternity ward stopped mothers from dying. He had the numbers. The profession laughed him out of the room, ran him into an asylum, and let him die there while the corpses kept stacking up exactly the way his data said they would. That is the lesson a labeled cross-section will never teach you: a body is not a quiet diagram you survive. It is a city full of factions, debts, and standoffs, and being right inside it has never once been the same thing as being believed.

The Biological Metropolis books your physiology as that city and hands you the gavel. This is Social Story Wrestling at body temperature: you pick up an organ, a cell, or a historical troublemaker, you perform its case out loud at the table, and the room decides whether the city buys you or riots.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Biological Metropolis Core Deck: 32 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" cards, featuring The Scorekeeper (the immune system running a ledger nobody else is allowed to audit), The Cortisol Architect (stress rebuilt as a contractor who never stops pouring concrete), and The River Body (you, reframed as moving water the whole city is plumbed into).
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the homeostasis roll that decides whether the city holds its balance or tips over. ATP tokens and inflammation markers are in the box.
- The City Roster: govern The Brain, negotiate with The Gut, answer to Ignaz Semmelweis and the Semmelweis Problem, and find out what Autoimmune and Cancer do the night a city turns on its own citizens.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
This deck is part of the Komik Kard Kult Klub. Grabbing it is not buying a frozen PDF. It is a standing seat in the city. Every future district, expansion, and new citizen in this cycle lands in your hands as a free update.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I'm a physician and artist. I would rather you knew your own body as a living, arguing place than memorized it as a diagram you lose by summer. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Learn it, play it, run your own metropolis. Want to support the craft? Every euro goes straight into drawing the next citizens and sharpening the mechanics. Free to share and adapt under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, never resold.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
Your body was never a diagram. It is a city, and tonight you hold the gavel.
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
